A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On the Separability of Information in Diffusion Models. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original Gaussian simulations, trained diffusion-model experiments, and image and latent-space analyses in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including Gaussian guidance experiments and analyses using MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Tiny ImageNet.

M1.justification: The entropy-matching formulation, CFG procedure, and semantic/perceptual split-loss autoencoder remain unchanged. The new analytical discussion and architecture disclosures do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic Gaussian data, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Tiny ImageNet with the same tasks and scenarios. The new discussion of higher resolutions adds no evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: The analytic Gaussian reference comparisons and VAE–DAE comparisons in Figures 14–15 are retained. Neither the newly cited studies nor the new CFG formula becomes an additional evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The existing Gaussian parameter sweeps, latent dimensions, partition-time scans, and evaluation quantities remain unchanged. v5 newly documents training and evaluation settings without establishing revisions to the previously used protocol.

E4.justification: The flattening and determinism tests, CFG-weight scans, reconstruction comparisons, latent visualizations, and partition-time analyses are retained. v5 adds explanations and qualifications without additional empirical diagnostic analyses.

E5.justification: The neural-entropy and MINDE estimators remain unchanged, and neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Monte Carlo batch and grid details document implementation of the existing estimates.

E6.justification: The plotted results and numerical summaries are unchanged. For example, Figure 16 retains CIFAR-10 neural entropy of 7776.2 and estimated mutual information of 7.5404 nats. The Gaussian and latent-probe findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a proposed analytic treatment of Gaussian CFG, including modified moments, a determinant expression for mutual information, and large-guidance scaling in Equations (60)–(66). Appendix A.1 additionally argues that divergent mutual information and total correlation survive basis changes. These are substantive mathematical additions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and principal conclusions retain the same claims about perceptual information dominating the information budget, its separation from class information, and the resulting explanation of CFG.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an interpretation extending separability to higher resolutions using existing Figure 16 results. Appendix E.3 now acknowledges that class information can remain in images without being captured by the perceptual latent. The conclusion also expands the renormalization-group connection.

D1.justification: New Table 1 supplies dataset-specific architecture, encoder, batch-size, learning-rate, and epoch details. Appendix E.3 adds Adam, the VP schedule, null-label marginal evaluation, and estimation using 500 test samples and 100 time points. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the existing hardware, framework, and code-access disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds information-flow studies by Stančević and collaborators, concurrent work by Handke et al., and comparisons with Xiang et al. and Chen et al. It positions external latent probes as complementary to internal-activation studies and adds a distinct Cotler–Rezchikov optimal-transport reference. The central novelty claim remains.

P1.justification: v5 makes local wording and terminology corrections, expands several explanations, updates affiliation and publication information, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the hyperparameter table and makes limited caption and page-layout changes, including a Figure 17 cross-reference in Figure 5's caption. The existing figure graphics, axes, legends, and plotted content are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 1 and the evaluation details substantially improve reproducibility, while Appendix E.3 appropriately qualifies the latent-probe inference. However, the new A.1 rotation argument is incorrect: its noiseless Gaussian example makes the orthogonal coordinate constant, giving zero mutual information rather than infinity. The new CFG derivation also identifies a score-defined Gaussian with the sampling endpoint without establishing that step. These documentation gains and mathematical problems leave the net quality change uncertain.
